title: LLM Inference: Temperature, Top-p, KV Cache
interviewAnswer: Temperature and top-p affect sampling randomness; the KV cache reuses attention keys/values from previous tokens to avoid recomputing the entire prefix during autoregressive generation.
why: Inference controls explain output randomness and runtime cost. Temperature/top-p affect token sampling, while KV cache and batching affect performance.
intuition: The model produces logits for the next token. Decoding converts logits to probabilities and selects a token; caching reuses attention states from previous tokens so generation does not recompute the whole history.
deepDive: Temperature rescales logits before softmax: lower values sharpen the distribution; higher values flatten it. Top-p samples from the smallest token set whose cumulative probability reaches p. Greedy decoding chooses the max token. KV cache stores prior key/value projections for autoregressive attention, reducing repeated compute but consuming memory proportional to layers, sequence length, batch and head dimensions.
math: p_i = softmax(z_i / T). Lower T → sharper distribution.
workedExample: For deterministic structured extraction, use low temperature and schema constraints. For creative generation, moderate sampling may help. Large context + many concurrent requests can become KV-cache-memory bound even if model weights fit comfortably.
code:
# conceptual generation settings
generate(temperature=0.2, top_p=0.9, max_new_tokens=300)
commonMistakes: Treating top-p and temperature as equivalent controls.
Ignoring KV-cache memory when estimating serving capacity.
production: Monitor time-to-first-token, tokens/sec, context length, KV-cache utilization and batching efficiency. Decode settings should be task-specific and regression-tested.
